question: What is the primary focus of epidemiology in healthcare?

options.A: Studying disease occurrence and distribution in populations
options.B: Managing hospital financial records and staff
options.C: Treating individual patients in a hospital ward
options.D: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs for common illnesses

explanation: Epidemiology looks at populations rather than single patients to understand patterns of illness. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h1)

question: A public health nurse uses epidemiological data to plan which community intervention?

options.A: Surgical removal of an individual appendix
options.B: A mass measles vaccination campaign for children
options.C: Ordering new hospital beds for the ward
options.D: Prescribing glasses for a single clinic patient

explanation: Population-level data guides community-wide preventive actions like mass immunizations. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h1)

question: What are the three components of the epidemiological triangle?
explanation: The classic epidemiological triangle consists of the agent, the host, and the environment. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h2)

question: Clearing stagnant bushes and draining pools around a village represents intervention aimed at which part of the triangle?
explanation: Environmental modifications alter external conditions to reduce vector breeding sites. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h2)

question: Which epidemiological measurement includes a specific unit of time in its calculation?
explanation: Rates measure how fast a disease occurs within a population over a specific time period. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h3)

question: Calculating the fraction of hospitalized children who suffered from severe malnutrition is an example of what measurement?
explanation: A proportion expresses a part of a whole group, with the affected individuals included in the total. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a descriptive epidemiological study?

options.A: To examine disease distribution by time, place, and person
options.B: To manufacture vaccines for emerging viral pathogens
options.C: To provide direct surgical treatment to infected patients
options.D: To test causal hypotheses through experimental clinical trials

explanation: Descriptive studies focus on person, place, and time characteristics without testing hypotheses. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h4)

question: A researcher follows a group of healthy smokers and non-smokers over ten years to compare lung cancer rates. What study type is this?
explanation: Cohort studies follow exposure groups forward in time to observe disease development. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h4)

question: Giving routine childhood immunizations at a primary health clinic represents which level of prevention?
explanation: Primary prevention stops a disease from occurring in the first place through measures like vaccination. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h5)

question: Screening healthy adults for high blood pressure during a community outreach program is an example of what level?
explanation: Screening detects disease early so treatment can start before severe complications arise. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h5)

question: What defines a disease outbreak in a community setting?

options.A: A single patient visits the clinic with a chronic illness
options.B: Medical staff run out of standard prescription medications
options.C: Laboratory equipment breaks down in the regional hospital
options.D: The number of reported cases exceeds normal expected levels

explanation: An outbreak occurs when disease frequency rises above the baseline expected baseline for that area. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h6)

question: What is the immediate action a clinic nurse should take upon noticing an unusual spike in acute watery diarrhea cases?

options.A: Refer all patients immediately to international travel agencies
options.B: Wait until the end of the month to compile routine reports
options.C: Report the cluster to local public health authorities for investigation
options.D: Advise the community to stop drinking any fluids entirely

explanation: Timely reporting triggers outbreak investigations and coordinated public health responses. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h6)

question: Which seasonal disease outbreak frequently affects parts of the Nigerian meningitis belt?
explanation: Meningitis outbreaks recur seasonally in the northern region of Nigeria, requiring close epidemiological surveillance. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h7)

question: How does local epidemiological data directly assist Nigerian community health nurses?

options.A: By calculating hospital catering costs for patient meals
options.B: By dictating architectural designs for new surgical suites
options.C: By helping anticipate seasonal disease patterns and target interventions
options.D: By determining individual staff salary scales in tertiary hospitals

explanation: Knowing local epidemiological trends allows nurses to prepare adequate resources before seasonal spikes occur. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h7)
